topic: A maintenance agreement is worth more than the job that created it.

slides.subtitle: (not the job that started it)
slides.scene: The ScaileAI field technician standing beside a wall mounted furnace in a clean utility room, one gloved hand resting on a completely blank white service tag hanging from a wire on the unit. All vehicles, buildings, doors and surfaces in shot have COMPLETELY BLANK panels with absolutely no writing, no company name, no logo, no lettering, no phone number and no graphics of any kind. No signage anywhere in the scene. There is NO text, no words, no numbers and no labels anywhere in the image.

caption:
Did you know the maintenance agreement is usually worth more than the job that created it?

A repair is one transaction with somebody who will forget you. An agreement is a reason to be in that house every year, a reason they call you first when something else breaks, and a business that is worth something if you ever sell it.

And the moment to offer one is not in a letter next spring. It is while you are standing there, having just fixed the thing, at the exact point where they like you most.

That window is about ten minutes wide and it closes when you drive away.

Most contractors know this and still do not do it, because remembering to ask at the right moment on a Thursday afternoon is a discipline problem, not a knowledge problem.

If you want to see what that looks like running on your own jobs, book a twenty minute walkthrough at scaileai.com.
